items.stem: A manufacturer identifies a defect in its finished prescription-drug lot while the entire lot remains under the firm's direct control; none has been released for sale or use. It removes and destroys the lot. Under 21 CFR 7.3, how is the action classified?

choices.text: Class I recall because every manufacturing defect creates an FDA recall.
choices.why: Incorrect. The FDA definition of a recall concerns marketed violative product; the lot never left the firm's direct control.

choices.text: Stock recovery, rather than a marketed-product recall.
choices.why: Correct. Section 7.3(k) defines stock recovery for unreleased product still directly controlled by the firm.

choices.text: Market withdrawal of a distributed drug.
choices.why: Incorrect. Market withdrawal applies to distributed product in the particular minor/no-violation circumstances.

choices.text: A pharmacy-to-pharmacy returned prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. No pharmacy dispensed or transferred product in the scenario.

items.novelty_rationale: FDA marketed-versus-never-released product classification, distinct from known Class I/II/III recall questions.

items.stem: DEA-REGISTERED REVERSE DISTRIBUTOR: A pharmacy transfers its own expired Schedule II stock to a properly registered reverse distributor for destruction. The reverse distributor records receipt on November 2, 2026. Under 21 CFR 1317.15, which post-receipt duties apply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Securely store the material under applicable federal controls until lawful disposition.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1317.15(c) requires secure storage or prompt authorized handling of controlled substances acquired by a reverse distributor.

choices.text: Treat completion of the original pharmacy's inventory deduction as permission to store the material indefinitely.
choices.why: Incorrect. A registrant's accounting does not waive the reverse distributor's 30-day destruction duty for destruction stock.

choices.text: Destroy or cause destruction within 30 calendar days of receipt for substances accepted for destruction.
choices.why: Correct. 21 CFR 1317.15(d) sets a 30-calendar-day deadline from the reverse distributor's receipt.

choices.text: Redirect shipment after receipt to any unregistered warehouse selected for convenience.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation requires the authorized registered location and controlled custody, not unregistered diversion.

items.citation: 21 CFR 1317.15(c)-(d) (registered reverse distributor storage and 30-calendar-day destruction)
items.novelty_rationale: Replaces duplicated pharmacy-owned vs ultimate-user inventory disposal already E30-050/E30-180 with the reverse distributor's own post-acquisition secure custody and exact 30-calendar-day destruction deadline.

items.stem: After a routine Massachusetts vaccine administration, a pharmacist documents the dose. The patient develops a mild sore arm that is not a listed required-report event or contraindication, and no separate serious reaction occurs. Which statements accurately distinguish MIIS and VAERS obligations? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The immunization itself must be reported to Massachusetts MIIS under the Board vaccine-administration policy.
choices.why: Correct. The 2025 Board policy §IV(G) requires pharmacy personnel administering vaccines to report vaccination information to MIIS.

choices.text: A report to VAERS can be encouraged for a clinically meaningful event even when causality is uncertain.
choices.why: Correct. CDC encourages voluntary reporting of clinically significant events regardless of proof that the vaccine caused them.

choices.text: Every isolated mild sore arm is a federally mandatory VAERS report under the VAERS Table.
choices.why: Incorrect. VAERS mandatory healthcare-provider reporting covers enumerated reportable events and manufacturer-listed contraindications, not every mild event.

choices.text: Submitting immunization data to MIIS also completes any required VAERS adverse-event report.
choices.why: Incorrect. MIIS immunization registry reporting is different from adverse-event reporting through VAERS.

items.citation: MA Board Policy 2023-02 revised 9/4/2025 §IV(G); CDC VAERS Healthcare Provider Reporting
items.novelty_rationale: MIIS recording and VAERS are distinct duties; separates legally mandated events from encouraged reporting.

items.stem: A pharmacist administers prescribed intramuscular naltrexone to an adult under Massachusetts DPH Circular DCP 26-03-124. Later the patient reports a non-serious suspected adverse reaction that did not require an ED visit. Under the circular, how should the pharmacist communicate it?

choices.text: File a mandatory VAERS report for the injection.
choices.why: Incorrect. VAERS applies to vaccination reports; naltrexone administration is not vaccination.

choices.text: Notify the prescriber only if a causal link has been proved by the FDA.
choices.why: Incorrect. DPH guidance calls for appropriate communication of reactions, not proof of pharmacologic causation first.

choices.text: Contact the prescriber after the next scheduled annual drug-utilization review.
choices.why: Incorrect. The DPH circular establishes a 24-hour communication recommendation for non-serious reactions.

choices.text: Communicate to the prescriber within 24 hours and document it.
choices.why: Correct. DCP 26-03-124 directs adverse reactions to be communicated within 24 hours, with event recording.

items.citation: MA DPH Circular DCP 26-03-124, p.4 Reporting Adverse Events and Record Keeping
items.novelty_rationale: Actual 2026 nonvaccine adverse-event communication, distinct from VAERS reporting.

items.stem: A 19-year-old has a lawful prescription for a single-dose intramuscular testosterone injection for gender-affirming care. A Massachusetts pharmacist has appropriate injection training, CPR and other DPH-required qualifications. No intravenous administration is planned. Does DCP 26-03-124 permit pharmacist administration under the stated facts?

choices.text: Yes, if the listed training, prescription and administration safeguards are met.
choices.why: Correct. The March 2026 circular adds testosterone for gender-affirming care; single-dose IM route and adult eligibility are met.

choices.text: No; only vaccines can be administered by Massachusetts pharmacists.
choices.why: Incorrect. Massachusetts DPH recognizes listed non-vaccine pharmacist administration pathways.

choices.text: No; only patients aged at least 21 may participate.
choices.why: Incorrect. The circular establishes 18 years or older, not 21.

choices.text: Yes, but only by converting the patient prescription into the pharmacy's DEA order form.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient administration under a valid prescription is distinct from ordering pharmacy Schedule II inventory.

items.citation: MA DPH Circular DCP 26-03-124, pp.1–3; M.G.L. c.94C §1
items.novelty_rationale: New testosterone gender-affirming IM authorization vs previously tested cabotegravir HIV PrEP injection.

items.stem: A pharmacist administers an eligible long-acting antipsychotic injection in a Massachusetts pharmacy under DPH Circular DCP 26-03-124. The patient has a life-threatening reaction needing emergency services and ED monitoring. What must the pharmacy do? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Wait until the next routine quarterly appointment before informing the prescriber.
choices.why: Incorrect. The severity triggers immediate reporting rather than ordinary non-serious 24-hour communication.

choices.text: Immediately notify the prescriber of the life-threatening event in addition to handling the medical emergency.
choices.why: Correct. DCP 26-03-124 requires immediate prescriber communication for life-threatening outcomes or ED treatment/monitoring.

choices.text: For a serious adverse drug event, also follow the applicable Board reporting requirements.
choices.why: Correct. DCP 26-03-124 states serious adverse drug events and events from dispensing errors remain reportable to the Board as applicable.

choices.text: Separately assess Board reporting only when the event satisfies 247 CMR 20.02 or another applicable rule.
choices.why: Correct. The DPH circular directs reporting to the Board in accordance with Board regulations. Section 20.02 has specific triggers, such as improper dispensing with serious injury/death or serious events involving drugs manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy; an ordinary injection reaction is not categorically reportable to the Board.

items.citation: MA DPH Circular DCP 26-03-124 pp.3–4 (immediate prescriber reporting, administration records); 247 CMR 20.02(1)–(2) (separate, limited Board reporting triggers)
items.novelty_rationale: Separates immediate prescriber notification for life-threatening post-injection reaction from circumstance-specific Board reporting under 247 CMR 20.02, without treating all reactions as automatically Board reportable.

items.stem: DEA POWER-OF-ATTORNEY REVIEW — a corporate pharmacy proposes authorizing a technician to sign Schedule II orders. The instrument is signed by the pharmacy's HR manager who is authorized to submit DEA registration applications but is NOT a corporate officer, together with the technician and two witnesses. Under the March 20, 2026 amendment to 21 CFR 1305.05, what is missing?

choices.text: Nothing; the last DEA registration application signer's authorization is the required statutory condition.
choices.why: Incorrect. DEA's 2026 revision removed that legacy application-signer pathway for POA execution.

choices.text: A pharmacist's personal DEA registration number on the form.
choices.why: Incorrect. The POA is granted on behalf of the corporate registrant; the problem is the grantor's actual corporate authority.

choices.text: Execution by a registrant-authorized corporate officer, partner, or individual registrant as applicable.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1305.05(d)(1) prescribes the eligible grantor; being an HR application submitter alone does not qualify.

choices.text: A third witness from the state Board of Registration in Pharmacy.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal POA rule requires two witnesses, not three.

items.novelty_rationale: Explicit 2026 correction eliminates superseded signer ambiguity; evaluates actual POA document signatures.

items.stem: DEA SCHEDULE II POWER OF ATTORNEY: A corporate officer, the designated attorney-in-fact, and two witnesses sign a properly prepared POA using verifiable electronic signatures; no ink signatures appear. No other defect exists. Under 21 CFR 1305.05(f), is the document valid with respect to signature format?

choices.text: It fails because both witnesses must sign in ink, although the corporate officer may sign electronically.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal provision permits electronic signatures by any or all of the persons required to sign.

choices.text: It can satisfy the signature-format rule; electronic signatures are allowed for the required signatories.
choices.why: Correct. 21 CFR 1305.05(f) explicitly permits electronic execution by any or all required POA signers, including witnesses.

choices.text: It is valid only if DEA preapproves every electronic signature as part of the registration application.
choices.why: Incorrect. A compliant executed POA is retained with order records; individual DEA preapproval is not a requirement of §1305.05(f).

choices.text: It fails because any electronic signature converts a paper Form 222 POA into a personal CSOS certificate.
choices.why: Incorrect. DEA recognizes electronically signed POAs separately from an individual CSOS signing certificate.

items.citation: 21 CFR 1305.05(d),(f); 84 FR 51371 (Sept. 30, 2019) (electronic-signature authorization retained after 91 FR 13499 Mar. 20 2026)
items.novelty_rationale: Replaces C108's near-identical 2026 non-officer revocation scenario with a separate §1305.05(f) signature-format issue for four electronically signed parties.

items.stem: A DEA-registered corporate pharmacy orders Schedule II medicines on DEA Form 222. Its licensed pharmacist manager is not a corporate officer and has never received a POA. A registered-company officer is present. Which federal signer conclusions are supported? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The corporate officer can sign under 21 CFR 1305.12(d) without a separate individual POA if authorized in that capacity.
choices.why: Correct. The 2026 rule permits corporate officers of the registrant to sign Form 222 directly.

choices.text: The MOR can sign based only on the title Manager of Record, even without POA or corporate-officer status.
choices.why: Incorrect. A professional or facility job title alone is not federal Form 222 signature authority.

choices.text: Every pharmacy technician is an automatic DEA Form 222 signer once hired.
choices.why: Incorrect. Employment does not create an individual POA or corporate officer status.

choices.text: The MOR could sign after receiving a valid executed POA meeting 1305.05.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1305.12(d) also permits an individual with a lawful POA to sign for the registrant.

items.novelty_rationale: Distinguishes corporate officer's direct signature, an MOR's lack of inherent authority, and a real POA.

items.stem: A pharmacy keeps executed DEA Forms 222, but files a technician's properly executed POA only in the individual's private home and refuses to produce it during a DEA inspection. What does 21 CFR 1305.05(a) require?

choices.text: The POA must be sent to DEA before each Form 222 is executed.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal regulations require retaining the POA with order files, not resubmitting it for each order.

choices.text: It is sufficient to tell DEA the name of the attorney-in-fact by telephone.
choices.why: Incorrect. An inspector can require the executed written/electronic POA and its documented validity.

choices.text: A POA may be discarded once the technician has signed the first controlled order.
choices.why: Incorrect. The POA retention period follows the signed orders and is not exhausted by first use.

choices.text: Retain the executed POA with relevant order files and make it inspectable.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1305.05(a) directly requires retention for the same period as orders bearing the attorney's signature and inspection availability.

items.novelty_rationale: New physical/document custody and inspection of POA, not employer personnel-file retention.

editorial_note: D058 replaced duplicated C108 revocation authority with electronic-signature-format rule; corrected D057 and D059 Federal Register document identifier from incorrect 2026-05525 to actual 2026-05482.
